name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent’s deterministic rules in a pre-commit hook. It cuts latency by blocking bad commits before they waste review time. Trade-off: extra setup effort upfront, but the long-term speed gain outweighs it.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t bad changes slipping through—it’s that "safe" is subjective. PR-Agent’s rules may block valid work if they’re too strict, or miss real issues if they’re too loose. A better alternative: run PR-Agent in CI only, where we can adjust thresholds without blocking developers. Settle it by testing both approaches on a sample of past commits and measuring false positives vs. false negatives.
